options: Not bringing objects to show parents is ordinary in a two-language home
Waiting is correct once any second language is in the house
Two languages do not remove pointing, showing, or turning to a name
No words in either language is the expected pattern when two languages are spoken
Brief eye contact means the wait is appropriate
correctAnswer: Two languages do not remove pointing, showing, or turning to a name
explanation: Two languages are the wrong explanation, because he does not point and does not turn to his name. Two languages do not remove pointing, showing, or turning to a name. No words in either language is the expected pattern when two languages are spoken is not, with the missing gestures. Brief eye contact means the wait is appropriate is a warning. Not bringing objects to show parents is ordinary in a two-language home is a missing skill. Waiting is correct once any second language is in the house does not explain the missing skills.
